candidates.description: a free and open source speech synthesizer for Russian and other languages
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# RHVoice

RHVoice is a free and open-source speech synthesizer.

## Features

### Speech synthesis method

RHVoice uses [statistical parametric synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_synthesis#HMM-based_synthesis).
It relies on existing open-source speech technologies (mainly
[HTS](https://hts.sp.nitech.ac.jp) and related software).

Voices are built from recordings of natural speech. They have small footprints,
because only statistical models are stored on users' computers. And though the
voices lack the naturalness of the synthesizers which generate speech by
combining segments of the recordings themselves, they are still very
intelligible and resemble the speakers who recorded the source material.

### Supported languages

Initially, RHVoice could speak only Russian. Now it also supports:

* American and Scottish English
* Brazilian Portuguese
* Esperanto
* Georgian
* Ukrainian
* Kyrgyz
* Tatar
* Macedonian
* Albanian
* Polish

In theory, it is possible to implement support for
other languages, if all the necessary resources can be found or
created.

### Synthesis example

If you want to listen to an example of speech synthesis, You can use the TTS
service on [this page](https://data2data.ru/tts/).

### Supported platforms

RHVoice supports the following platforms:

* Windows (prebuilt binaries is available in documentation)
* GNU/Linux (building instructions and packaging status
  can be found in "Compiling instructions" section of documentation.
* Android (can be installed thru
  [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.github.olga_yakovleva.rhvoice.android/)
  or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.github.olga_yakovleva.rhvoice.android)

It is compatible with standard text-to-speech interfaces on these platforms:
SAPI5 on Windows, [Speech Dispatcher](https://devel.freebsoft.org/speechd) on
GNU/Linux and Android's text-to-speech APIs. It can also be used by the
[NVDA screen reader](https://www.nvaccess.org) directly (the driver is provided
by RHVoice itself).

## Documentation

All prebuild binaries packages, main
and legal information and more
are available in three languages:

* [English](doc/en/index.md)
* [Русский](doc/ru/index.md)
* [Українська](doc/ua/index.md)

## Community

### Official

* [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/RHVoice/RHVoice/discussions/)
* [Mailing list](https://groups.io/g/RHVoice-rus) (Russian)

### Unofficial

* IRC channel: `#rhvoice` at [irc.libera.chat](ircs://irc.libera.chat:6

Nuxt LLMs automatically generates [`llms.txt` markdown documentation](https://llmstxt.org/) for your Nuxt application.  It provides runtime hooks to collect data from various sources (CMS, Nuxt Content, etc.) and generate structured documentation in a text-based format.

- [✨  Release Notes](/CHANGELOG.md)
<!-- - [🏀 Online playground](https://stackblitz.com/github/your-org/nuxt-llms?file=playground%2Fapp.vue) -->
<!-- - [📖  Documentation](https://example.com) -->

## Features

- Generates & prerenders `/llms.txt` automatically
- Generate & prerenders `/llms-full.txt` when enabled
- Customizable sections directly from your `nuxt.config.ts`
- Integrates with Nuxt modules and your application via the runtime hooks system

## Quick Setup

1. Install the module:

```bash
npm i nuxt-llms
```

2. Register `nuxt-llms` in your `nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-llms']
})
```

3. Configure your application details:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-llms'],
  llms: {
    domain: 'https://example.com',
    title: 'My Application',
    description: 'My Application Description',
    sections: [
      {
        title: 'Section 1',
        description: 'Section 1 Description',
        links: [
          {
            title: 'Link 1',
            description: 'Link 1 Description',
            href: '/link-1',
          },
          {
            title: 'Link 2',
            description: 'Link 2 Description',
            href: '/link-2',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
})
```

That's it! You can visit `/llms.txt` to see the generated documentation ✨

## Options

- `domain`(required): The domain of the application
- `title`: The title of the application, will be displayed at the top of the documentation
- `description`: The description of the application, will be displayed at the top of the documentation right after the title
- `sections`: The sections of the documentation.
  Section are consisted of a title, one or more paragraphs of description and possibly a list of links.
  Each section is an object with the following properties:

  - `desc

# ShrimpReel

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Built by [浅水虾 (qianshuixia)](https://x.com/qianshuixia2026).

An open-source template for "one photo → an AI video that follows a viral template" SaaS sites. Every trending keyword gets its own site: create a repo from this template, change the config, copy and media, and ship. Everything runs on Cloudflare: Workers + D1 + R2 + KV + Queues + Rate Limiting + Cron Triggers.

> Status: the full flow works locally (unit tests + Playwright e2e). It has not been deployed as a production site yet; [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) lists what has and hasn't been verified against real services. Code comments, ROADMAP and `docs/` are currently in Chinese.

- Frontend/SSR: TanStack Start (React 19) + Tailwind 4. English at `/`, Chinese at `/zh`.
- API: Hono (`/api/*`, `/media/*`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, IndexNow key file); entry point `src/server.ts`.
- Payments: Waffo Pancake (default) or Dodo Payments, both Merchants of Record. `mock` is for local dev and e2e only.
- Video: fal.ai queue API (`mock` for local dev and e2e).
- Included:
  - Users and credits: Google sign-in (including One Tap), credit packs and a credit ledger, dashboard (videos, billing, settings, account deletion, data export); billing shows amounts paid and refunded, orders and the ledger load page by page, and every order has a printable detail page (tax invoices come from the payment provider).
  - Orders and generation: partial and full refunds that claw back credits, a generation queue with a dead-letter queue, credits returned automatically on failure.
  - Growth: first- and last-touch attribution (UTM and ad click IDs), a visit → sign-up → checkout → paid → generate funnel, GA4 events behind a consent banner.
  - Admin: overview (including provider cost and gross margin), users, orders, generations, takedowns, contact messages, payment events, emails, audit log, reports and order CSV.
    - Users: filter by status, role and paying, sort by sign-up, last login or credits; the detail page shows total paid, generation stats, orders, the credit ledger and admin actions on that user.
    - Orders: search by order id, email or provider transaction id; the detail page merges payment webhooks, credit changes, admin actions and emails into one timeline, with refund and mark-paid actions.
    - Generations: search by job id, email or provider request id.
  - Transactional email: credits added, video ready, generation failed and refunded, takedown receipts

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Lights-on software factory boilerplate for Claude Code

A starting point for running a lights-on software factory with Claude Code. Based on the setup developed for
[Votito](https://www.votito.com), where the orchestrator reduced token spend compared to bare-bones Claude workflow execution by around 80%. 

See [gojko.net/slides/202609-gotocph.pdf](https://gojko.net/slides/202609-gotocph.pdf) for a quick overview.

## What is in this repostory?

The purpose of this repository is to act both as a simple boilerplate setup for
new projects, and as an educational demonstration of the core concepts of
software factories:

This repository provides setup for:

1. A sandbox/container for running Claude Code in a secure environment, sharing only the workspace directory with the host. See [CONTAINER.md](CONTAINER.md) for more information.
2. A deterministic bash command regulator, to reduce approval fatigue and ensure agents execute the commands allowed by project-specific rules. The regulator performs a deep-inspection of bash commands and provides automated approve/deny with instructions on what to do instead if blocked. See [REGULATOR.md](REGULATOR.md) for more information. Ask Claude to add more custom rules each time it asks you for approval.
3. A deterministic linter-based feedback system for enforcing custom domain-specific rules, to help reduce human involvement in code review. A `PostToolUse` hook runs the linter on every JavaScript file Claude edits, and guides the agents to avoid common mistakes with helpful error messages. Ask Claude to write more custom rules each time you find yourself providing repetitive design/code feedback. Ask Claude to implement custom eslint language parsers for HTML/CSS/other file types. See [LINTER-HOOK.md](LINTER-HOOK.md) for more information.
4. A basic planning/implementation workflow. This is a trivial example intentionally kept simple to demonstrate the format and serve as a foundation for the orchestrator. You should probably replace it with your own commands or more complex rules. See [WORKFLOW.md](WORKFLOW.md) for more information.
5. A deterministic multi-agent Claude workflow script generator. Based on the plan produced by the implementation workflow, it creates Claude workflow scripts, structures testing and gates and avoids wasting inference tokens on the mechanical part of workflow orchestration. It speeds up workflow creation and moves many common workflow orchestration tasks from inference (LLM) to deterministi

candidates.description: Tell your coding agent which dependencies changed after its training cutoff. Diffs types and changelogs, writes a short block into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
Install · Example · How it works · Results · Changelog

Coding agents learn libraries from training data that stops at a cutoff date. When your project pins newer versions, the agent writes code for the old API: `maxSteps` against AI SDK 7, `required_error` against zod 4, `middleware.ts` against Next 16. stalemap finds the dependencies that changed after your model's training cutoff and tells the agent what changed, in three ways: - **Notes:** a short, ranked list of changes written into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, so the agent reads it before it starts. - **Edit-time guard:** after each edit, the project's own type-check. If the code uses an API that changed after the cutoff, the agent gets the compiler error and the matching note (or the release-note or upgrade-guide section that explains it) right away. It also reports the code that still compiles but uses something that moved. - **`search_changes`:** an MCP tool the agent can ask in its own words, such as "resolve alias in next.config", to get the matching changes with their sources. It works for JavaScript and TypeScript projects, with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode or any MCP client. **In a blind, pre-registered benchmark** of 66 tasks built from changes released after June 2026, `claude-sonnet-5-5` agents passed **89%** of sessions with stalemap, against **68%** with no help and **73%** with a plain `tsc --

candidates.description: A Claude Code skill for clean, honest dashboard UI: KPI tiles, charts, date pickers, ranked lists, states, layouts and a screenshot QA pass. Distilled from 127 shipped dashboards.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Dashboard Design: a Claude Code skill for clean, honest dashboards

Give your coding agent the taste of a senior product designer for data screens, on the web or in SwiftUI. This
skill teaches it to build,
redesign and **critique** analytics, revenue and metrics dashboards: KPI tiles, charts, comparison periods, ranked
breakdowns, date range pickers, filters, insights, empty states, wide and phone layouts. It ends every job with a
screenshot QA pass, so it judges what is on the screen rather than what is in the code.

![A dashboard built with the skill: KPI strip with a selected tile, revenue chart with round ticks, slim-bar breakdowns](docs/images/dashboard.jpg)

It was distilled from **127 shipped dashboard screens** (analytics tools, revenue dashboards, design systems,
design galleries), a full teardown of one revenue-analytics product, and a real redesign where every rule here was
broken once, caught on a screenshot, and fixed.

## What it changes

| Instead of | The agent builds |
|---|---|
| A tinted block behind every list row | A slim 3 px share bar along the row's edge |
| An underline marking the selected tile | A soft tinted fill with a faint ring |
| Native `21/09/2026 📅` date inputs | A popover calendar: soft band, solid end days, "12 days" + Apply |
| A narrow column floating on a wide monitor | A wide mode that adds columns as the screen grows |
| A red **−100%** when 1 sale became 0 | A quiet grey "was 1" |
| Axis ticks like 2,103 and 1,402 | Round ticks: 0, 1k, 2k |
| Sparklines with 60 empty days and a spike | Sparklines on the same window as the chart |
| An insight card repeating a tile | Insights only when they say something new |
| Sideways-scrolling tabs on phones | A menu grid and tabs that shrink |

### Before / after on an ultrawide screen

![Before: a narrow column with empty bands on both sides](docs/images/wide-before.jpg)
![After: the page grows and the four breakdowns sit in one row](docs/images/wide-after.jpg)

### Components

| | |
|---|---|
| ![KPI tiles with the selected one as a soft tinted fill](docs/images/kpi-tiles.jpg) | ![Ranked lists with slim share bars](docs/images/ranked-lists.jpg) |
| ![One-month range calendar with a soft band between solid end days](docs/images/range-calendar.jpg) | ![Phone navigation as a menu grid](docs/images/phone-menu.jpg) |

## Install

**As a Claude Code plugin**

```
/plugin marketplace add abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
/plugin install dashboard-design@dashboard-design-sk

Run `npm run test` first, use tiny sizes, and review every config value before using `npm start`. ## Requirements - Node.js `>=20.10` - npm The bot uses the non-beta CLOB package `@polymarket/clob-client-v2` for trading and the public Data API for wallet activity polling. Edit `.env`: ## Live Trading ```bash POLYMARKET_CLOB_HOST=https://clob.polymarket.com POLYMARKET_CHAIN_ID=137 POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE=POLY_1271 POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY=0x... POLYMARKET_DEPOSIT_WALLET=0x... ``` `POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE` accepts `EOA`, `POLY_PROXY`, `POLY_GNOSIS_SAFE`, or `POLY_1271`. For new deposit-wallet users, `POLY_1271` is usually the right value. For EOA trading, `POLYMARKET_DEPOSIT_WALLET` can be omitted. You can also provide existing L2 credentials to avoid deriving them on startup: ```bash CLOB_API_KEY=... CLOB_SECRET=... CLOB_PASS_PHRASE=... ``` The executor uses `createAndPostMarketOrder`. Before live trading, your trading wallet still needs funds and the required Polymarket approvals; this bot does not try to deploy wallets or auto-approve spending. ## Copy Modes Fixed mode: ```bash COPY_MODE=fixed FIXED_BUY_AMOUNT_USD=5 FIXED_SELL_AMOUNT_USD=5 ``` Percentage mode: ```bash COPY_MODE=percentage COPY_PERCENTAGE=0.10 ``` For buys, percentage mode copies a percentage of the followed trade's USD notional.
